author: Jcarrill0
subject: [Paladin] Team 5-Paladin Dungeon builds
content_md:
So back on "old" project servers, I enjoyed doing end-game dungeons using all Paladins.

we had a group of 5 Paladins that was Talent-Spec'd to compliment each other.

while the runs were all successful, I wanted to see if it could be done again.

Here is the 5 Paladin builds:

[The Tankadin](https://classicdb.ch/?talent#sxVzZVhxIxzVoV0L) - Protection Paladin. Judgement of Justice, Blessing of Sanctuary, Resistance Aura (Fire/Shadow/Frost).
[The Healadin](https://classicdb.ch/?talent#sVxubgstgMt00h) - Holy Paladin. Lasting-Judgement of Light, Improved-Blessing of Wisdom, Improved-Concentration Aura.
[The Reckadin](https://classicdb.ch/?talent#sZVGtzc0xZVf0tRfk) - Hybrid Reckoning Paladin. Improved-Judgement of Crusader, Blessing of Kings, Improved-Retribution Aura.
[The Ret Pally](https://classicdb.ch/?talent#sE0zZVhZgf0trcqo) - Retribution Paladin. Improved-Judgement of Crusader, Improved-Blessing of Might, Sancity Aura.
[The Shockadin](https://classicdb.ch/?talent#sEVurxstxhZV) - Spell Power Paladin. Lasting-Judgement of Wisdom, Blessing of Light, Improved-Devotion Aura (With Libram).
please note: these Talent-Specs were designed only for the purpose of clearing all the end-game dungeons and while they were all successful and fun, it's not recommended for Hardcore Raid or Hardcore PvP.

the end-Goal was to get a joint 10-Man UBRS using the Paladins as well, but that never happened.

Thoughts? Please reply with you comments/Concerns/Rants below.

Keep it civil please!

subject: Turtle WoW Paladin Guide - 1.17.2
content_md:
This isn't designed to hit EVERY single nail on the head, but a simple guide for TWoW Paladins.
 - If You Have Suggestions, Drop a Comment!

 --==  BASIC INFO ==--
Paladins are not the fastest leveling class early on, but can make up for it towards the end, and are very versatile being able to perform all 3 group roles.
<https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?spells=7.2#0+2+1>
Spells not listed, Holy Strike R2(8), R3(16), R4(24), R5(32), R6 (40), R7 (48), R8 (56)

 --== BEST RACE  ==--
PvE Melee (Tank/Ret): Human
Sword/Mace Specialization: You must increase your hit chance and reduce dodge/block/glance.
Note: +3 weapons skill is equal to approximately 1% chance to hit
Perception now also grants 2% increased physical and spell critical strike chance for the duration.

PvE Caster: High Elf
Quel’dorei Meditation: Recovers 10% of mana activates after a 1.5-second cast Cooldown 3 minutes.
Note: As a Healer this is HUGE for dungeons/raids, with less downtime in general
Enchanting Specialization: +10 Enchanting is just another benefit to the race.

PvP: Dwarf
Stoneform : While active, grants immunity to Bleed, Poison, and Disease effects.  In addition, Armor increased by 10%.  Lasts 8 sec.

 --== TURTLE WOW NOTABLE CHANGES ==--
Turtle WoW Paladins have (3) new abilities;

Holy Strike (Lv 4): Strike your target for X to Y Holy damage, restoring Z health and Z mana to you and your party.

Crusader Strike (Lv 8): A strike that causes X% weapon damage plus an additional Y and grants you a stack of Zeal. Zeal stacks up to 3 times. Lasts 30 sec.

Zeal increases your attack and casting speed by 3%.

Paladins should make use of (Equip adds X Damage to melee attacks) as these all trigger Judge of Wisdom (JoW). These can also CRIT based on spell crit and proc Vengeance. (List Below)

Hand of Reckoning: Taunts the target to attack you, causing a high threat.

Consecration: Baseline, Lv 20
Prot Talent Shield Specialization: Restore 2% Mana When Block Occurs 5 sec cd.
Divine Shield now reduces all damage dealt by 50% instead of reducing attack speed by 100%.
Ret Talent Seal of Command Not Unlocked Till Lv 30.

Blessing of Freedom, Blessing of Sacrifice and Blessing of Protection are now Hand of Freedom, Hand of Sacrifice and Hand of Protection. They do not remove active blessings, but are exclusive to each other (for example, the target can’t have Hand of Freedom and Hand of Sacrifice from one Paladin at the same time.)

All ranks of Blessing of Might, Blessing of Wisdom, Blessing of Kings, Blessing of Salvation, Blessing of Light and Blessing of Sanctuary now have a 10 minute duration.

All ranks of Greater Blessing of Might, Greater Blessing of Wisdom, Greater Blessing of Kings, Greater Blessing of Salvation, Greater Blessing of Light and Greater Blessing of Sanctuary now have a 30 minute duration.

Additional Changes Can Be Seen Here:
<https://turtlecraft.gg/#/paladin>
[viewtopic.php?p=102974#p102969](https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=102974#p102969)

 --== PALADIN RECOMMENDED SKILLS WHILE LEVELING  ==--

Seal of Righteousness 3.4 or Faster
Seal of Command 3.5 of Slower (ONLY USE/TRAIN Rank 1 To Conserve Mana till 60, Same Weapon DMG)
Seal of Wisdom Lv 18/28/38
Seal of Light Lv 28
Seal of Justice (Skip)
Seal of the Crusader (Skip)

Judgment
Crusader Strike:
Holy Strike: Main Ability All Specs 100% Holy damage attack (Free) cost.
Divine Protection
Hammer of Justice
Purify
Lay on Hands
Holy Light
Flash of Light
Divine Shield
Cleanse
Hammer of Wrath
Summon Warhorse
Summon Charger
Consecration - Trained Baseline Lv 20
Blessing of Sanctuary - (If Your Prot)
Righteous Fury - (If Your Prot + Plan To Dungeon & Leveling in a group)
Redemption - (Skip - If Hardcore)
Divine Intervention - (Skip - If Hardcore)

Hand of Protection
Hand of Freedom
Blessing of Wisdom
Blessing of Might

Devotion Aura - (Lv 16 Swap To Retribution Aura)
Retribution Aura - Main Aura From 16+
Concentration Aura - Main Healing Aura 22+
SKIP Resist Auras - But Situational.

 --== PALADIN ADDONS ==--

 1. Swing Timer
<https://github.com/EinBaum/SP_SwingTimer>

 2. No Error Sound Effects (No More "I'm not ready yet, and all that other noise").
<https://github.com/mrrosh/NoErrorSounds>

 3. Turtle Version 1.17.2 PallyPower - an easy-to-use interface that allows you to set your blessings and automatically check for missing buffs.
<https://github.com/madScripting/PallyPower-TurtleWoW>

 3.  ETL - Exp Per hour/time til level addon
<https://github.com/shirsig/ETL>

 4.  Outfitter - is an equipment management addon that gives you fast access to multiple outfits.
<https://github.com/CosminPOP/Outfitter>

 5.  SuperMacro - provides a very much improved interface for macros
<https://github.com/Monteo/SuperMacro>

 --== MACROS ==--

Example 1:  Begins Auto Attack, cast CS
/script if (not PlayerFrame.inCombat) then AttackTarget() end
/cast Crusader Strike

Example 2: Begins Auto Attack, then checks for SoR, if no SoR casts SoR, else uses CS.
/script if (not PlayerFrame.inCombat) then AttackTarget() end
/script if buffed("Seal of Righteousness") then CastSpellByName("Crusader Strike") else if not buffed("Seal of Righteousness") then CastSpellByName("Seal of Righteousness") end end

Example 3: Begins Auto Attack, checks for SoR, if No SoR casts SoR, else judges JoR
/script if (not PlayerFrame.inCombat) then AttackTarget() end
/script if buffed("Seal of Righteousness") then CastSpellByName("Judgement") else if not buffed("Seal of Righteousness") then CastSpellByName("Seal of Righteousness") end end

Can edit above with different Seals etc.

 --== Basic Leveling Rotation ==--
Level 1-30 (Judging too often can speed kill time, but also eats more mana)
Use Seal of Righteousness (SoR)
Use Blessing of Might/Wisdom (as needed)
Use Max Rank Holy Strike (It's FREE Recovers Mana Cost + JoW)
Consecration 2+ Targets.
Finish off With Judge of Righteousness.
Reseal and go again

Level 20+ (Prot) Open World
Use Blessing of Sanctuary
Judging too often can speed kill time, but also eats more mana)
Use Max Rank Holy Strike (It's FREE Recovers Mana Cost + JoW)
Use Seal of Righteousness (SoR) or Seal of Wisdom/Light(SoW/L) in AoE 3+ Situations.
Auto Till Low
 - If Redoubt Procs, Cast Holy Shield(HS) - (Blocks will Regen Cost of HS)
Finish off With Judge of Righteousness if using.
Reseal and go again

Level 30+ (Prot) Dungeon
Use Blessing of Sanctuary
Judging too often can speed kill time, but also eats more mana)
Use Max Rank Holy Strike (It's FREE Recovers Mana Cost + JoW)
 -> Use Seal of Wisdom(SoW) 100%
Judge SoW, Reseal SoW
Drop Highest Rank Consecrate, followed by R1
If Redoubt Procs, Cast Holy Shield(HS) - (Blocks will Regen Cost of HS)
Auto Till Low
Reseal and go again
Bosses JoW, can use SoR for more threat, but high-rank consecrate+hs is generally enough.

Level 30+ (Ret)
Judging too often can speed kill time, but also eats more mana)
Use Blessing of Might/Wis
Use Seal of Command R1 (SoC)
Use Max Rank Holy Strike (It's FREE Recovers Mana Cost + JoW)
Auto Till Low
Can cast Judgement between Autos, finish off With Judge of Command (JoC)
Why?- R1 SoC is pretty inexpensive so judging for that extra dmg between autos is fine vs SoR.
Reseal and go again
A harder Target can be Stunned/Judged for more damage/burst.

 --== PROFESSIONS ==--

--== TURTLE WOW NOTABLE CHANGES ==--
Turtle WoW Paladins have (3) new abilities;

Holy Strike (Lv 4): Strike your target for X to Y Holy damage, restoring Z health and Z mana to you and your party.

Crusader Strike (Lv 8): A strike that causes X% weapon damage plus an additional Y and grants you a stack of Zeal. Zeal stacks up to 3 times. Lasts 30 sec.

Zeal increases your attack and casting speed by 3%.

Paladins should make use of (Equip adds X Damage to melee attacks) as these all trigger Judge of Wisdom (JoW). These can also CRIT based on spell crit and proc Vengeance. (List Below)

Hand of Reckoning: Taunts the target to attack you, causing a high threat.

Consecration: Baseline, Lv 20
Prot Talent Shield Specialization: Restore 2% Mana When Block Occurs 5 sec cd.
Divine Shield now reduces all damage dealt by 50% instead of reducing attack speed by 100%.
Ret Talent Seal of Command Not Unlocked Till Lv 30.

Blessing of Freedom, Blessing of Sacrifice and Blessing of Protection are now Hand of Freedom, Hand of Sacrifice and Hand of Protection. They do not remove active blessings, but are exclusive to each other (for example, the target can’t have Hand of Freedom and Hand of Sacrifice from one Paladin at the same time.)

All ranks of Blessing of Might, Blessing of Wisdom, Blessing of Kings, Blessing of Salvation, Blessing of Light and Blessing of Sanctuary now have a 10 minute duration.

All ranks of Greater Blessing of Might, Greater Blessing of Wisdom, Greater Blessing of Kings, Greater Blessing of Salvation, Greater Blessing of Light and Greater Blessing of Sanctuary now have a 30 minute duration.

--== Basic Leveling Rotation ==--
Level 1-30 (Judging too often can speed kill time, but also eats more mana)
Use Seal of Righteousness (SoR)
Use Blessing of Might/Wisdom (as needed)
Use Max Rank Holy Strike (It's FREE Recovers Mana Cost + JoW)
Consecration 2+ Targets.
Finish off With Judge of Righteousness.
Reseal and go again

Level 20+ (Prot) Open World
Use Blessing of Sanctuary
Judging too often can speed kill time, but also eats more mana)
Use Max Rank Holy Strike (It's FREE Recovers Mana Cost + JoW)
Use Seal of Righteousness (SoR) or Seal of Wisdom/Light(SoW/L) in AoE 3+ Situations.
Auto Till Low
- If Redoubt Procs, Cast Holy Shield(HS) - (Blocks will Regen Cost of HS)
Finish off With Judge of Righteousness if using.
Reseal and go again

Level 30+ (Prot) Dungeon
Use Blessing of Sanctuary
Judging too often can speed kill time, but also eats more mana)
Use Max Rank Holy Strike (It's FREE Recovers Mana Cost + JoW)
-> Use Seal of Wisdom(SoW) 100%
Judge SoW, Reseal SoW
Drop Highest Rank Consecrate, followed by R1
If Redoubt Procs, Cast Holy Shield(HS) - (Blocks will Regen Cost of HS)
Auto Till Low
Reseal and go again
Bosses JoW, can use SoR for more threat, but high-rank consecrate+hs is generally enough.


Level 30+ (Ret)
Judging too often can speed kill time, but also eats more mana)
Use Blessing of Might/Wis
Use Seal of Command R1 (SoC)
Use Max Rank Holy Strike (It's FREE Recovers Mana Cost + JoW)
Auto Till Low
Can cast Judgement between Autos, finish off With Judge of Command (JoC)
Why?- R1 SoC is pretty inexpensive so judging for that extra dmg between autos is fine vs SoR.
Reseal and go again
A harder Target can be Stunned/Judged for more damage/burst.

I'm aware of the differences between macros and addons. The actual functional code of my rogue's macro is written in raw lua (specifically so it could be shared with people with 0 addon dependencies), the point was that i had enough space to spare even after that to fit in #showtooltip and /startattack after the fact, and that was just to make it look nice on my hotbar and to kick off autoattacking.

For reference, here is an entire assassination rogue's rotation in raw lua that fits in one macro without any #showtooltip or /startattack:

/run c=CastSpellByName p=GetComboPoints() g=GetPlayerBuff t=GetPlayerBuffTexture s=strfind if p==5 then c("Rupture")end
/run i=0 m=0 while not (g(i)==-1) do if (s(t(g(i)),"INV_Sword_31")) then m=1 end i=i+1 end if m==0 then if p<5 then c("Envenom")end end
/run i=0 m=0 while not (g(i)==-1) do if (s(t(g(i)),"Ability_Rogue_SliceDice")) then m=1 end i=i+1 end if m==0 then if p<5 then c("Slice and Dice")end end
/run c("Noxious Assault")
/run if (not PlayerFrame.inCombat) then AttackTarget() end

A better way to track CS/HS would be by actually checking the buff duration remaining. If there's less than 6 seconds left on holy strength, use holy strike, otherwise use crusader strike. If you're in prot, then just check if zeal is at 3 stacks, if it's not use CS, if it is check if it has less than 6 seconds left, in which case refresh it, otherwise just use HS

You're assuming that melee healing Paladins are strictly for "noobs," but that's a narrow take. The melee healing archetype isn’t inherently bad—it just has a higher execution requirement and demands proper encounter design and team synergy. Yes, they take more damage and face more interrupts, but they also bring powerful utility to the frontline: instant spot healing, blessings, and the ability to weave in melee attacks for mana sustain or proc effects.

The idea that ranged Paladins are the only "pro" option ignores the fact that some top players have optimized melee healing builds and found success in coordinated groups where positioning, interrupts, and utility management are tightly controlled. Not every healer should be a turret at 40 yards spamming heals.

As for gear—yes, the Kara 40 set seems built with the melee-healing playstyle in mind, but that doesn't mean it's "for noobs." It simply supports an alternative build path. And frankly, diversity in viable builds is good for the game. A ranged-only healing meta creates stagnation. Giving Paladins both a melee and ranged option isn’t just catering to skill level—it’s offering playstyle choice. And the best players will make either work depending on comp, fight mechanics, and strategy.

author: Tankmeister
subject: Feedback on holy and prot paladin after leveling to 60
content_md:
(*this post was formatted using AI for better readability)*

I’ve played Paladin since retail Vanilla, through Wrath, and into Cataclysm. First, I want to commend the Turtle WoW team - this is by far the most fun version of Paladin I’ve experienced in WoW. After leveling to max and spending a lot of time in dungeons (and a few raids), here’s my feedback:

Protection

 **Positives**

Seals and Judgements finally feel impactful. Choosing the right seal/judgement in the moment feels somewhat strategical.

The Reckoning redesign is fantastic. Having it proc immediately, and on block, makes sense thematically and feels rewarding.

Having a taunt is just good.

Converting some blessings into hand spells is a welcome quality-of-life change.

 **Mixed Feelings**

Bulwark of the Righteous is a great addition with both offensive and defensive utility. That said, a 5-minute cooldown feels like a lot. I’d personally prefer a slightly weaker version that could be used more often.

Holy Strike and Crusader Strike are excellent concepts but currently feel underutilized. Right now, I just use Crusader Strike to keep Zeal up, and otherwise Holy Strike. I’d love to see more meaningful choice regarding these two abilities:

Holy Strike: a supportive option - perhaps by providing a short party buff (e.g. a 6-second damage boost). Or just significantly increasing the healing done.

Crusader Strike: a survival tool, enhancing my defenses (also for 6 seconds).

Right now, the Holy Strike heal is simply too weak to matter and Crusader Strike just feels like a chore you have to keep doing.

 **Negatives**

Eye for an Eye should be available to Prot again. It was the only real tool against casters in PvP, and it fit the Paladin fantasy very well.

Holy

I’ve never really played as a healer in WoW before. Standing at the back spamming heals never appealed to me. But Turtle’s melee-healer design tempted me to try Holy, and I’m surprised by how much I enjoy it.

 **Positives**

The melee healing playstyle is fun and engaging. Even if I’m not dealing huge damage, being in the fight and seeing damage numbers alongside heals just feels better.

 **Mixed Feelings**

The interplay between Holy Strike and Crusader Strike works better here than in Prot. Timing Crusader Strike to refresh Holy Shock vs. using Holy Strike for healing/mana management feels meaningful. But again, Holy Strike’s heal (even with Blessed Strikes) is far too weak. I’d prefer if Holy Strike had a more impactful heal, and compensating with lowering healing from other spells. That would add a conscious choice between “healing one vs. healing many” to the gameplay.

 **Negatives**

Daybreak feels underwhelming and uninteresting. It could be much more engaging if it were an activated ability. For example, alongside its current effect, it could make your next heal a guaranteed crit. This would also synergize nicely with Holy Strike, since the only time it feels impactful is when it crits and procs Daybreak.

Closing Thoughts

Overall, I think Paladin on Turtle WoW has had a lot of great improvements. Fun, unique, and closer to what I always wished the class had been in retail. However, it leaves a lot more to be desired and improved upon, and I hope the dev team continues to realize this hidden potential.
content_html:
(this post was formatted using AI for better readability)

I’ve played Paladin since retail Vanilla, through Wrath, and into Cataclysm. First, I want to commend the Turtle WoW team - this is by far the most fun version of Paladin I’ve experienced in WoW. After leveling to max and spending a lot of time in dungeons (and a few raids), here’s my feedback:

Protection

Positives

Seals and Judgements finally feel impactful. Choosing the right seal/judgement in the moment feels somewhat strategical.

The Reckoning redesign is fantastic. Having it proc immediately, and on block, makes sense thematically and feels rewarding.

Having a taunt is just good.

Converting some blessings into hand spells is a welcome quality-of-life change.

Mixed Feelings

Bulwark of the Righteous is a great addition with both offensive and defensive utility. That said, a 5-minute cooldown feels like a lot. I’d personally prefer a slightly weaker version that could be used more often.

Holy Strike and Crusader Strike are excellent concepts but currently feel underutilized. Right now, I just use Crusader Strike to keep Zeal up, and otherwise Holy Strike. I’d love to see more meaningful choice regarding these two abilities:

Holy Strike: a supportive option - perhaps by providing a short party buff (e.g. a 6-second damage boost). Or just significantly increasing the healing done.

Crusader Strike: a survival tool, enhancing my defenses (also for 6 seconds).

Right now, the Holy Strike heal is simply too weak to matter and Crusader Strike just feels like a chore you have to keep doing.

Negatives

Eye for an Eye should be available to Prot again. It was the only real tool against casters in PvP, and it fit the Paladin fantasy very well.

Holy

I’ve never really played as a healer in WoW before. Standing at the back spamming heals never appealed to me. But Turtle’s melee-healer design tempted me to try Holy, and I’m surprised by how much I enjoy it.

Positives

The melee healing playstyle is fun and engaging. Even if I’m not dealing huge damage, being in the fight and seeing damage numbers alongside heals just feels better.

Mixed Feelings

The interplay between Holy Strike and Crusader Strike works better here than in Prot. Timing Crusader Strike to refresh Holy Shock vs. using Holy Strike for healing/mana management feels meaningful. But again, Holy Strike’s heal (even with Blessed Strikes) is far too weak. I’d prefer if Holy Strike had a more impactful heal, and compensating with lowering healing from other spells. That would add a conscious choice between “healing one vs. healing many” to the gameplay.

Negatives

Daybreak feels underwhelming and uninteresting. It could be much more engaging if it were an activated ability. For example, alongside its current effect, it could make your next heal a guaranteed crit. This would also synergize nicely with Holy Strike, since the only time it feels impactful is when it crits and procs Daybreak.

Closing Thoughts

Overall, I think Paladin on Turtle WoW has had a lot of great improvements. Fun, unique, and closer to what I always wished the class had been in retail. However, it leaves a lot more to be desired and improved upon, and I hope the dev team continues to realize this hidden potential.

Hi friend, I haven't yet entered dungeons, as I said I am speaking solely for the leveling experience (which is a big element of vanilla wow hence I feel servers that are vanilla-esque ought to pay attention to its wellbeing) - for that leveling experience, I feel like Crusader Strike is too much as it is.
Judgement of Righteousness at level 10 deals about 25 holy damage. It is a very good nuke at 10 seconds cooldown.
Plagued by the fact that is the only on demand nuke of the class for long (or forever for Ret) and that casting it means abolishing your combat system (your seals). Furthermore you can't even cast it if someone decides to constantly dispel your combat system (your seals).

Undoubtedly paladins needed some improvement and the careful introduction of an extra on demand damaging ability was long overdue.

Holy strike deals about the same damage as judgement while being on a 6s cooldown, it is in melee range but it is independent and doesn't require an active seal, neither does it consume one. Even if it were on a 10s cooldown (like judgement) it would effectively mean double the amount of damage and on demand strikes.

A definite improvement right? The numbers are quite clear.
Now taking it to 6s right off the bat is kind of questionable but borderline swallow-able. But enter Crusader Strike doing 31+35% weapon damage, so about 35-38, is kind of too much. It makes me considering not using it while leveling even. That on top of a great passive buff it gives.

 **Imo to preserve the leveling experience:**
- Crusader Strike + Holy Strike should start on an 8/10s cooldown.

- Crusader Strike should be 100-110% weapon damage always plus its zeal effect.

- Both Strikes through their respective tree 5 pointer boooster should receive 0.4/0.8s cooldown reduction (taking them back to 6s with the 5 talents).

- Through the same talents receive as much of a damage boost as necessary to preserve end game DPS to what it is now or what is always necessary for the specs to be viable (as you said it's fine)

Currently, Auto Attack + SoC procc + Crusader Strike can already almost kill questmobs with a bit of critluck in one go. If you add another Proc to it there is a good chance your questing, farming and pvp encounter end in the first second you get into melee. This is exasturbated once you  get swing increases such as wings of the timelord, hoj or other similar effects. Especially with WF in the mix. That might be fun for a few hours as a milestone to reach, but it considerably dulls gameplay down afterwards.

To give you an example of how much (by current balance figures unnecessary-) power that is:
You could increase the damage of ret paladins seals by 50%(!) and it would still be less strong.

On hit modifiers such as wf & seals dont mix well with instant attacks. Which is why shaman and pala are nightmares to balance, and always will be.

author: Atreidon
subject: Re: Another Paladin fanfic talents rework
content_md:
Lets start with the ideas i like.

Evil is a point of view is a great talent both flavorwise and gameplaywise if you ask me. As it taps into the more sinister aspects of blind faith, befitting a ret paladin.
It should however be limited to damaging abilities. Paladin should not gain access to a widely useable fear spell. Particularly not in conjunction with any other of the massive buffs that you intend for the class.

Consecration being useful as a healspell would be a great addition to healpaladin, as they struggle from not having enough buttons to press. Making consecration be useful for them would be great. However it definitely needs some tweaking. As "all friendly targets" in some fights can mean upwards of 1k hps per paladin.
Id rather have it say "up to x friendly targets inside the area get healed for half that amount". Keeping its usefulnes while limiting the abuse potential of just stacking the raid in a ball and dropping some consecrations. (Especially since tank and retpalas can come and pick the talent uo with very little downsides).
Or simply limit it to the paladins group.

Searing light might be fun to enable a more spellcaster type paladin. But with the numbers given, it is undoubtably a meme. Which i think is good. Paladin has some playstiles. He doesnt need to be good at range too.
Hereim just worrying about tankshaman syndrome where over time it will get buffed to an unreasonable degree because people adore a meme spec. Creating a lot of problems in the future in other game areas (particularly pvp as was the case with shaman and pala in the past)

Now for the stuff i dont like at all
Bullwark of the righteous
Is hitting people with your shield cool as hell? of course!
Is it also brutal and slightly dirty and undoubtably a warrior ability? Also yes!
With the current threat and dps numbers, tank paladin does not need to pilfer the one cool thing prot warrior has in his arsenal.

Northshire abbey training replacing precision and the removal of imp hand of reckoning leave paladin with wanting 17% spellhit for their taunt. Warrior and Druids both have secondary taunt effects (aoe taunt/mocking blow) in a pinch if their taunt misses. Paladin (and Shaman) dont have that. They need their taunt to be more reliable. And the respective spellhit talents are vital for them being reliable at taunting.

Radiance & the change to divine shield i am absolutely not a fan of. It gives tank paladin access to the single hardest hitting aoe ability in the game.
And at the same time it takes away ita debuff cleansing properties. The best thing abour current divine shield!

Then there is the mess that is conviction into holy cleave into vengeance.
Why am i forced by prerequisite talent to improve them both? These abilities are sharing cd. If they have separate talents, I should have the option to invest in one and not the other!

It also is a 15 pt chain that you basically have to take towards the end of the tree. Ensuring you have to invest far more than 31 points and overinvest into the tree (something that has sadly become all too common with the reworked talent trees)

Another one that ruffles my feather is the buff to imp. Hammer of justice. Base cd is 60 seconds. With the talent it goes to 40. With the pvp setbonus a further 10 seconds and libram of the justicar nabs another 5 seconds.

As 25 second cd 20y ranged stun that lasts 6 seconds... No thanks
When suggesting talents please ensure you are aware of what interactions that are already in the game you are impacting.

author: Maxe71
subject: Suggestion: Seals & Blessings Are Too Easily Dispelled (Need a Talent-Based Solution)
content_md:
Hi fellow Paladins and Turtle WoW team,

I’d like to bring up an issue that many Retribution and Holy Paladins feel very strongly about, especially in PvP:
our Seals and Blessings are extremely easy to dispel, and this leaves the class unable to function during combat.
Paladins are heavily dependent on both Blessings and Seals to do anything — pressure, utility, mobility, damage, healing flow, you name it.

But right now:
One single dispel can remove Blessing of Freedom, Blessing of Protection, or Blessing of Sacrifice instantly.
Seals are removed just as easily, shutting down core abilities like Judgement, burst windows, or defensive play.
Classes with strong dispel tools can lock a Paladin out of almost everything with very little effort.
Because of this, Paladins often end up in situations where they simply cannot play their class, despite using their tools correctly.

Proposed Solution: A Talent That Protects Seals & Blessings
My suggestion is to introduce a new talent or position in one of the Paladin trees that:
Makes the Paladin’s own Seals and Blessings immune to dispel,
OR
Gives them a very high chance to resist dispels (e.g., 50–75%),
OR
Applies a buff that temporarily prevents dispel effects after casting a Seal or Blessing.
This would give Paladins a fair chance to actually use their toolkit without being shut down completely by a single dispel spam.
It wouldn’t make us overpowered — it would simply let us function.

Final Thoughts

Just my two cents to improve class balance and gameplay feel.
I love the server and appreciate all the work the creators have done.
Thanks for reading, and I’d be glad to hear the thoughts of other Paladins and the dev team.

content_md:
I understand the point about dispels being the counter to buffs, just like kicks counter casts.
But there’s an important difference here:

A Paladin without seals or blessings doesn’t just get “countered”—he loses his entire kit.
Other classes don’t become “unplayable” when you remove a single component of their rotation.

A Priest doesn’t just stand still spamming dispel—he applies DoTs, Mana Burn, SW:D pressure, so while he dispels my seal, I’m also rotting at the same time.

Same with Shamans: even if purge now has a CD, they still keep massive burst windows (WF + shocks + CL) that a Paladin has no tools to smooth out, except bubble—which is purely defensive, and cuts our offense in half while it’s active.

My point was never that “counters shouldn’t exist,” but that no other class becomes completely neutered by a dispel the way Paladins do. Something that gives partial resistance, or reduced dispel success, or a talent that stabilizes at least one core seal, would prevent the class from collapsing the moment a dispeller is present.

Just my 2 cents, fellow Paladins—and devs.

author: Maxe71
subject: Re: Suggestion: Seals & Blessings Are Too Easily Dispelled (Need a Talent-Based Solution)
content_md:
I see your point, and I agree that dispellers should counter buff-based classes — but the situation for Paladins is not exactly equal when compared to other classes being unbuffed.

A Priest doesn’t just sit there spamming Dispel: while he removes your Seal, he also loads you with DoTs, so you’re forced to spend your GCDs refreshing Seals and cleansing, while he’s still dealing damage in the background.
Same for Shamans: yes, Purge now has a CD, but their burst window is extremely high and the Paladin has no real way to stabilize it except Bubble — which is a purely defensive trade and completely shuts down your own offense.

Other classes unbuffed don’t lose their entire kit or identity. A Warrior without Battle Shout is still a Warrior. A Rogue without Slice and Dice is still fully lethal. A Mage without Arcane Intellect still casts.

A Paladin without his Seal literally stops functioning, because both pressure and utility are tied to buffs that can be removed instantly.

I’m not asking for uncounterable Blessings or Freedoms — those should absolutely remain dispellable.
But Seals getting removed so easily creates a situation where the Paladin loses access to his core rotation entirely.

A talent that gives partial Seal resistance (not immunity) or a chance to resist dispels could help keep the class functional without removing its intended counters.

Just my condensed thoughts — respect for your points, fellow paladin.

content_md:
I understand the counterplay argument, but there are a few practical issues worth noting from the Retribution Paladin perspective.

First, refreshing seals while also dispelling DoTs, slows, poisons or magic debuffs quickly becomes unsustainable, especially considering that a Ret paladin’s mana pool is much smaller than most other mana users. Trading GCDs with a priest isn’t equal when the priest can also pressure you with DoTs while you burn mana simply trying to stay operational.

Second, if you try to actually play the class as intended — applying a seal, using Judgment for its effect, and re-applying the seal — against constant dispel spam this becomes almost impossible. On top of that, with a 2H swing timer of 3.5+ seconds, losing even one window because a seal was stripped at the wrong moment can literally delete your entire damage cycle.

I don’t think this is about removing counters or giving paladins “no downsides”, but about acknowledging that when almost many classes can strip seals instantly while still dealing full pressure, Ret ends up spending most of the fight not dealing damage, but trying to function.

Just my perspective as someone actually playing it in PvP.

Have fun, blessed one

content_md:
So, I will continue in RP version:

Brothers and sisters of the Light,

I speak not as someone seeking to twist the scales of balance, nor as a herald of some “super-paladin”, but simply as a veteran of the path — one who has walked Azeroth since the closed beta of 2004, and who carried the banner of the Paladin even before that, back in the age of Sanctuary on Diablo II.

Over the years I’ve seen our class rise, fall, break, mend, and be reinvented a dozen times.
Turtle WoW is, sincerely, one of the finest reinterpretations I’ve ever played.
The work of the devs shines through, and many long-forgotten archetypes — including Protection — finally breathe again. For that, my thanks are genuine.

My point was never to demand immunity, superiority, or to drown other classes in weakness.
It was simply to place on the table a different perspective, born from actual play experience:
as Retribution — with low mana, long swing timers, and a kit that is entirely built on Seals & Blessings — being dispelled repeatedly can sometimes invalidate not “my strength”, but the basic rhythm that the class fantasy is designed around.

That’s not a call for domination… merely an observation from the field.

If the idea of “undispellable Seals” is too extreme, fair enough — a cooldown on purge/dispell could be an alternative, or even something lighter, as long as it keeps the gameplay flowing instead of freezing it with GCD-trading.

I appreciate your views, even when they clash with mine.
We stand in the same hall, after all — discussing, adjusting, improving the world we all share.

Blessings upon you all, and may your weapon never miss its mark.
— Sybril, Knight-Captain of the Light

**⟨Battle Chronicle of Sybril, Knight-Captain of the Light⟩**

The wind howled over the red dust of the Barrens as I faced him — the orc shaman with eyes like storm clouds and a grin full of tusks.

We circled.

He raised his hands first.
Lightning cracked.
I stepped forward, planting my boots, letting the Holy Light coil through my gauntlets.

He laughed.
I did not.

I sealed my blade with Command, the metal humming like a hymn.
The first swing landed clean — the Light burst, blinding white.
He staggered, but his totems erupted around him like roots of the earth itself.

A Grounding Totem cracked and fizzled my Judgement into harmless sparks.
A Stoneclaw tried to clutch my ankles.
He leapt back, hands already weaving the next spell.

I charged through.
Hammer of Justice landed like a cathedral bell — and the world froze for a heartbeat.

But the shaman broke free with a snarl, calling the wind.
Purge ripped the blessings from my armor like pages torn from scripture.
The next instant he was already upon me, Stormstrike flashing, tearing Light and flesh.

I answered with Holy Strike, golden fire bursting across the valley.
My strength surged, Armor gleamed, the earth cracked beneath us.

We traded blows —
his Frost Shock against my resolve,
my Seal of Righteousness bursting with every strike,
his Earthbind slowing my steps,
my Consecration searing runed footprints in the soil.

He called the storm.
I called the Light.

When our forces collided, the air itself seemed to hold its breath —
rain sizzling against holy fire,
totems shattering under consecrated steel,
the echo of Judgement rolling across the plains like thunder in a chapel.

In the end neither of us fell.
He bowed.
I nodded.

And the storm died with dignity.

 **— Sybril, Knight-Captain of the Light**

The most important thing as a tank, no matter the class you play, keybind the raidmarks. Especially the "Skull" icon.

Put it on a mob (preferably a healer or caster mob)
When you pull everything, concentrate on tanking all other mobs. Dps will kill skull first and you can focus on grabbing all the other mobs with ease.

author: Reploidrocsa
subject: Re: How to Tank
content_md:
One trick is often overlooked and helps all tanks.

Make a macro or a keybinding to mark a target with skull (optional a 2nd one marking X). Unless clueless or trolling, most damage dealers will go to marked targets, making your tanking job easier and giving you enough time to grab the entire pull.

You can use it to prio dangerous targets, or when the order isn't relevant to ensure focus to one single mob.

Best decision i've made for tanking in general.

On a more specific case, paladins can either body pull, use dynamites or ask any ranged to do the pull for them. If someone pulls for you, make sure you drop a consecration to intercept, and always hide behind a corner if the pull includes ranged mobs

author: Akos1896
subject: Re: How to Tank
content_md:
I'm not a pala expert but had a prot pala.
Trying to give some tricks.
 1. Make sure righteous fury is always on. If you died, first thing is to reapply it.
 2. Keybind raid icons as others said.
 3. For blessing, go for the best for the party, unless you are undergeared. You can salv them, it's okay. Specially salv big damage DPS unless they are totally ok with pulling the mob from you.
 4. You see a pack. Put up skull. Run in (won't talk about range pulls and body pulls here). Prepare the seal and judge your main target with it (usually wisdom so you have a passive mana battery on the battlefield). Then strike (if I remember, holy strike was usually better). Ensure holy shield is always on. You can keep threat by tabbing between the mobs. If there are 3+ mobs, consec makes wonders.
 5. Go for ret aura for more consistent threat unless you feel super squishy, then devotion aura it is.
 6. As you have problems with range, always be mindful what you run into. Accidentall multipulls can happen. Worst case: have some ez-throw grenades for range pull or ask someone to range pull. Body pull comes with experience.
 7. Don't be afraid of failing. All tanks have a bit of learning curve, but pala is an easier and very rewarding one. Just remember: blessings are up on everyone, aura is up, righteous fury is up, seal is always up, holy shield always up, judgment at pull followed up by strike and keep tabbing, consec anytime but mostly in case of 3+ mobs.
 8. With SP gear you can eventually use different ranks of consec, considering spell downgrades.

Have fun.

author: SvenS2
subject: Re: How to Tank
content_md:
A good habit is when you pull mobs, to always position them so that your dps is attacking them from behind. This helps achieve 2 things:

 1- Your physical dps won't lose on damage, as mobs and players can't parry, dodge or block when attacked from behind.

 2 - Mobs that run away when low on HP always run in the opposite direction of their last aggro target, which in this case would be you, the tank. Doing so will prevent the mob from accidentally pulling other packs by accident.

The real issue here is that Retribution isn't suffering from 'low numbers' - it’s suffering from disruptive and anti-synergistic mechanics. Tweaking a few percentages here and there won't change the fact that the spec is fundamentally fighting itself.

I'm relatively new to Turtle WoW, but I've spent an absurd amount of time on WoW in the past 19 or so years. Looking at the current state of the class, even with the custom changes, this feels like an underpowered version of the TBC ret pala, which had its fair share of troubles even back then.

Beyond the numbers and the horrendous amount of micro-timers we're forced to watch and maintain, the combat flow feels sluggish, heavy, and definitely not engaging in terms of fun. We are stuck with an archaic resource management system and a lack of real synergy between our strikes, making the gameplay feel cumbersome rather than rewarding. We don’t need 'more' of a clunky system; we need a few surgical mechanical tweaks to make the ret pala actually enjoyable to play and, ultimately, more viable for those of us pushing the AP-based holy fighter.

I’ll probably open a dedicated thread soon to share some of my ideas on how to address these bottlenecks, hoping for some healthy community discussion/constructive criticism

Either it does really good single target DPS but we are fine with it being bad on multi target fights, or we give it some sort of cleave ability, or as a third option we make them useful to have in a raid group. This could be done by turning sanctity aura from 10% holy damage increase to 3% damage increase to everyone in the group similar to the feral druid buff or trueshot aura.

Sure, it would bring a little something to the raid - and there's more to Wow than raids only - but it’s a massive net loss for the Paladin.

I'll die on this hill, ret pala needs mechanical tweaks. Moving numbers is not gonna do any good.

author: Draykomanuel
subject: Holy paladin needs changes
content_md: Hello, I'm a WoW player with over 20 years of experience as a Holy Paladin. I've played the class since 2005 through all its expansions. I'm a PvE and PvP player and have seen all the class changes over the years. Having said that, I'd like to give my humble opinion regarding the melee Holy Paladin. I see that some want to force the Holy Paladin to heal in melee, and I understand that there might be pressure from players who don't know the class or want to innovate with it. The Holy Paladin never worked and doesn't work in melee; it's a healer like any other, with ranged abilities that you have to know how to use. I know you want the Holy Paladin to heal in an area, but for that, you only need to give it the one ability that I think is the best for a Paladin to heal in an area without losing its essence. The ability is called Beacon of Light. This ability was added in the Wrath of the Lich King version, and it was very good, allowing the Paladin to maintain its essence and heal multiple members of its party simultaneously. That's speaking about PvE. Now... Speaking of PvP, they should restore the full damage of Holy Shock. Many of us want to play Shockadin in PvP, and it's not fair that other classes can do their full DPS while Holy Paladins can't be Shockadin. I hope you'll consider my small opinion and that it can bring about a change for the better for Holy Paladins. Thank you all! And may the light bless you.

author: Ellifta

content_md:
You talk about two things in this post, both of them are incorrect. Holy paladins are the best healers in the server at the moment by a big shot thanks to their melee healing ability. It works great, too great in fact that the best healers in the server are all paladins. It absolutely works and boosts your HPS massively, also synchronizes with how your talents push you towards wearing plate. >30% of my healing in Kara40 comes from melee healing at the moment, and this is also the case for any paladin up top with me.

Here are some scenarios that you can greatly benefit from holy strike as a holy paladin after you spec into blessed strike talent:
 -- ANY TIME raid wide damage happens, such as Majordomo fight, Lucifron fight after curses go out, Sulfuras, Magmadar when fires start hurting people, Shazzrah when curses go out (doesn't incur spell lock btw), Ragnaros 2nd phase, everytime a trash mob does AoE damage like dog fire breath or elemental charge.
 - Razorgore immediately after he does stomp, Vaelstratz on CD, trash packs on CD basically, Broodlord post stomp, Firemaw non stop, Flamegorr whenever he enrages and starts doing AoE damage
 - Every trash pack in AQ40, whenever Prophet Skeram does AoE arcane explosion, anytime the bug trio or viscidus shoots poison bolts, non stop use holy strike on Sartura especially against the boss herself, popcorn phase in Ouro,
 - Anytime Anub does knockback on ranged, anytime Faerlina does fire or poison around herself, Maexxna when spiders come out, whenever Grobbulus does poison spew on tank or shoots slime, at the beginning of Gluth fight, non stop on Thaddius in Thaddius phase, non stop on Loatheb fight, non stop on Sapphiron and KT
 - Holy strike right after blood moon goes out on Keeeper Gnarlmoon, holy strike whenever arcane rain happens on top of Ley watcher AND whenever adds to an AoE explosion, on CD on Anomolous and Medivh, everytime Bishop does shadow bolt AoE, non stop when killing Knight, on CD AND changing sides between Kruul's 4 second melee timer, during add phase of Sanv, Meph and 2nd phase of Rupturan.

There's infinitely more places holy paladin shines by using holy strike, these are some of the ones that come into my mind that you can incorporate into your playstyle. You need to be in melee, yes, even for fights like Grobbulus, Echo of Medivh, KT, fire drakes in BWL etc.

Melee healing holy paladin is the most fun healer has ever been in WoW and it is several expansions ahead of other healer classes purely on fun factor. It is so good in fact that nobody spoke against the massive nerf holy paladin is getting next patch, because we all know it deserves it, and I sincerely hope priests overtake us on raw effective healing because we have so much utility compared to them.

As for holy shock, holy paladin is already mega OP in PvP, I'd know because I'm R13 with 46k HKS playing hpala 90% of the time. It doesn't need any offensive abilities to be good, it is already the best class in the PvP scene at the moment.

People like you are the reason why paladin players get a bad rep, you somehow manage to complain the most powerful healer and PvP class is bad and doesn't work. The truth couldn't be further from what you posted. The only reason I stopped playing PvP is because I felt bad for whoever was going against me in AB.

Source: ![Image](https://i.ibb.co/zTHfG48s/imagess.png)

content_html:
You talk about two things in this post, both of them are incorrect. Holy paladins are the best healers in the server at the moment by a big shot thanks to their melee healing ability. It works great, too great in fact that the best healers in the server are all paladins. It absolutely works and boosts your HPS massively, also synchronizes with how your talents push you towards wearing plate. >30% of my healing in Kara40 comes from melee healing at the moment, and this is also the case for any paladin up top with me.

Here are some scenarios that you can greatly benefit from holy strike as a holy paladin after you spec into blessed strike talent:
-- ANY TIME raid wide damage happens, such as Majordomo fight, Lucifron fight after curses go out, Sulfuras, Magmadar when fires start hurting people, Shazzrah when curses go out (doesn't incur spell lock btw), Ragnaros 2nd phase, everytime a trash mob does AoE damage like dog fire breath or elemental charge.
- Razorgore immediately after he does stomp, Vaelstratz on CD, trash packs on CD basically, Broodlord post stomp, Firemaw non stop, Flamegorr whenever he enrages and starts doing AoE damage
- Every trash pack in AQ40, whenever Prophet Skeram does AoE arcane explosion, anytime the bug trio or viscidus shoots poison bolts, non stop use holy strike on Sartura especially against the boss herself, popcorn phase in Ouro,
- Anytime Anub does knockback on ranged, anytime Faerlina does fire or poison around herself, Maexxna when spiders come out, whenever Grobbulus does poison spew on tank or shoots slime, at the beginning of Gluth fight, non stop on Thaddius in Thaddius phase, non stop on Loatheb fight, non stop on Sapphiron and KT
- Holy strike right after blood moon goes out on Keeeper Gnarlmoon, holy strike whenever arcane rain happens on top of Ley watcher AND whenever adds to an AoE explosion, on CD on Anomolous and Medivh, everytime Bishop does shadow bolt AoE, non stop when killing Knight, on CD AND changing sides between Kruul's 4 second melee timer, during add phase of Sanv, Meph and 2nd phase of Rupturan.

There's infinitely more places holy paladin shines by using holy strike, these are some of the ones that come into my mind that you can incorporate into your playstyle. You need to be in melee, yes, even for fights like Grobbulus, Echo of Medivh, KT, fire drakes in BWL etc.

Melee healing holy paladin is the most fun healer has ever been in WoW and it is several expansions ahead of other healer classes purely on fun factor. It is so good in fact that nobody spoke against the massive nerf holy paladin is getting next patch, because we all know it deserves it, and I sincerely hope priests overtake us on raw effective healing because we have so much utility compared to them.

As for holy shock, holy paladin is already mega OP in PvP, I'd know because I'm R13 with 46k HKS playing hpala 90% of the time. It doesn't need any offensive abilities to be good, it is already the best class in the PvP scene at the moment.

People like you are the reason why paladin players get a bad rep, you somehow manage to complain the most powerful healer and PvP class is bad and doesn't work. The truth couldn't be further from what you posted. The only reason I stopped playing PvP is because I felt bad for whoever was going against me in AB.
